findings.title: AtliQ warrants it solely owns PipeKit; the signed Northwind contract appears to assign PipeKit to Northwind
findings.quote: Supplier warrants that it is the sole owner of all intellectual property rights in PipeKit, that it is entitled to grant the rights set out in § 6.2, and that PipeKit and its use under this Agreement do not infringe any rights of third parties.
findings.explanation: The Rheinwerk draft builds the project on PipeKit (§6.1) and has AtliQ promise it is the sole owner and free to license it (§6.3), backed by an indemnity (§6.4). The signed Northwind contract says all IP in the Deliverables, expressly including tools, frameworks, libraries and pre-existing materials incorporated into them, vests in Northwind on payment of each Milestone, and SOW-1 says PipeKit is incorporated into the delivered pipeline. Neither Northwind clause carves PipeKit out or gives AtliQ a licence back. Whether Northwind now owns PipeKit as delivered, and whether AtliQ can still give the §6.3 promise, is a possible conflict, for counsel. Pranav's remark that PipeKit can be reused 'like we did for Northwind' is the reuse that Northwind's text may already have given away.

register_refs.quote: All Intellectual Property Rights in the Deliverables, including any software, tools, frameworks, libraries and pre-existing materials incorporated into the Deliverables, shall vest in the Client absolutely upon payment of the Charges for the relevant Milestone.
PipeKit will be configured and extended for the Client and incorporated into the delivered pipeline as its ingestion and orchestration layer.

findings.title: PipeKit licence is perpetual, irrevocable, covers modification, and reaches Rheinwerk's customers and sub-licensees
findings.quote: Supplier hereby grants Client a perpetual, irrevocable, non-exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free right to use, reproduce, modify and operate PipeKit as incorporated in the Work Results, for the purposes of operating, maintaining and further developing the Platform, including for the benefit of Client's customers.
findings.explanation: The draft does not assign PipeKit: §6.5 excludes it from what Rheinwerk acquires, and AtliQ keeps ownership. What it does give is a permanent, non-revocable right to modify PipeKit and use it for Rheinwerk's own customers, and to sub-license it to Rheinwerk's affiliates and service providers (§6.2). AtliQ's other signed deals limit the licence to using PipeKit-type materials inside the Deliverable (Crestline) or for the client's internal business purposes (Lakeshore draft). Karandeep's checklist says 'we keep our own stuff'; this licence lets Rheinwerk's customers run it. The commercial value of that is a decision for a person.

findings.title: Annex 1 (scope) and Annex 3 (data processing agreement with transfer clauses) are referred to but not in the file
findings.quote: the Parties shall conclude the Data Processing Agreement pursuant to Art. 28 GDPR attached as Annex 3, which forms an integral part of this Agreement.
findings.explanation: The draft says the Art. 28 GDPR data processing agreement and the EU Standard Contractual Clauses for transfers to India are in Annex 3, and that the detailed specification is in Annex 1. Neither annex is in the file; only Annex 2 (milestones and fees) is. Acceptance (§5.1), the warranty (§7.1) and the milestone definitions (§1.3) all depend on Annex 1, and the data protection terms AtliQ would be bound by sit in Annex 3. Those terms cannot be tested until the annexes are supplied.

findings.title: German law and exclusive Munich courts; AtliQ's usual position for the Pvt Ltd is Indian law
findings.quote: The exclusive place of jurisdiction for all disputes arising out of or in connection with this Agreement shall be Munich, Germany.
findings.explanation: Karandeep's checklist is Indian law for the Pvt Ltd. This draft uses German law (§14.1) and Munich courts only (§14.2); there is no arbitration option. AtliQ has accepted a non-Indian law for the Pvt Ltd twice before, each time with a recorded reason (English law at Northwind, DIFC law at Al Noor). The Kessler Mobility German deal was lost over unlimited liability, not governing law, and the liability terms here are different (see checks passed). Whether to accept German law and courts is a recorded-decision item.
